Greece reports six airspace violations by two Turkish UAVs in Aegean

4 October 2026 · Northeastern / central Aegean · Greek-reported Turkish UAVs

Greek-authority-reported Turkish UAV airspace violations

On 4 October 2026 Greece’s Hellenic National Defence General Staff reported that two Turkish UAVs had been active over the northeastern and central Aegean, recording six violations of national airspace and three infringements of the Athens flight information region (FIR). OnAlert relayed the account that evening; exact sites and sortie times were not published.

The Turkish identification and the description of the flights as national-airspace violations are Greek military assessments, and the Greek-Turkish airspace dispute remains relevant. The drones’ models were not specified, and no coordinates or tracks have been independently verified. The figures measure different things and are not separate incidents.

The drones were identified and intercepted under standard procedures. No armed aircraft, engagements, shoot-downs, crashes, casualties or damage were reported.
